title: Computer Memory Hierarchy, Storage Units & Types

units.size: 8 Bits (Fundamental unit representing one alphanumeric character)

ram.name: Random Access Memory (RAM)
ram.characteristics: Primary main memory; directly accessible by CPU; read and write; VOLATILE (contents lost instantly when power is cut).

types.mechanism: Built with flip-flops (transistors). Does NOT need periodic refreshing. Faster, generates less heat, more expensive. Used in CPU Cache.
Built with capacitors and transistors. Electric charge leaks, so it REQUIRES periodic refreshing thousands of times per second. Slower, cheaper, higher density. Used as main system RAM.

rom.name: Read Only Memory (ROM)
rom.characteristics: Permanent memory containing bootstrap loader and basic firmware; read-only during normal operation; NON-VOLATILE (contents retained even when power is off).

types.details: Hardwired during manufacturing; cannot be altered.
Manufactured blank; can be programmed once using a PROM burner (One-Time Programmable).
Can be erased by exposing the chip to strong Ultraviolet (UV) light through a quartz window for 15-20 minutes, then reprogrammed.
Can be erased and rewritten electrically byte-by-byte without removing from circuit. Modern computer BIOS/UEFI chips are EEPROM / Flash memory.

bios_and_booting.bios: Basic Input/Output System stored in ROM. Performs Power-On Self-Test (POST) upon system startup to verify CPU, RAM, keyboard, and disk drives are functioning before loading the OS kernel.

booting_types.details: Starting a computer from completely powered-off state by turning on the physical power switch.
Restarting a computer that is already powered on (via Ctrl+Alt+Del or OS Restart command). Does not cut power to the motherboard.

virtual_memory.definition: An OS memory management technique where a portion of secondary storage (hard disk/SSD) is treated as an extension of physical RAM when RAM runs out of space.

terms.details: A fixed-size block of virtual memory (typically 4 KB).
A fixed-size block of physical RAM.
Occurs when a program requests a memory page that is currently not in physical RAM, triggering OS to load it from disk.
A degraded system condition where CPU spends more time swapping pages between RAM and disk than executing user programs.
